review_method: Direct visual inspection of three initial PNGs through view_image, with source/actual case metrics read independently.
intents: Actual h,b,y sample trajectories and absolute residuals to frozen S8 numerical reference.
Per-case normalized fixed-gate comparison with preserved incomplete/failure semantics.
Recorded solver work and single-run process elapsed diagnostics.

semantic_findings.finding: rtol1e-8 and1e-10 curves overlap because recorded errors/counters coincide; readers could miss one tolerance.
semantic_findings.action: Retain actual curves and state explicitly in captions; no order estimate.

semantic_findings.finding: Both arms have identical RHS call counts at each tolerance; orange curve covers blue.
semantic_findings.action: Use distinguishable markers at identical coordinates and explicitly report equal counts.

layout_findings.finding: Figure1 completion suptitle overlaps shared legend.
layout_findings.action: Move completion count into panel(a) title and remove suptitle.

layout_findings.finding: Figure3 lower-left legend overlays Jacobian-count line.

bounds_questions.question: Are residuals divided by a physical variable that may cross zero?
bounds_questions.answer: No. h,b,y differences use absolute residuals and retain zeros on a symlog scale.

bounds_questions.question: Does the reference claim exact continuum truth?
bounds_questions.answer: No. Labels and caption identify frozen S8 numerical samples.

bounds_questions.question: Are colors normalized to the unchanged preregistered gates?
bounds_questions.answer: Yes. Denominators are read from PREREGISTRATION.json and printed per column.

bounds_questions.question: Are missing or stopped histories represented as success?
bounds_questions.answer: No. Helper requires recorded assessment completion, raw completion and process exit0; partial metrics have p labels.

bounds_questions.question: Does timing establish portable speedup?
bounds_questions.answer: No. Process elapsed is single-run, host-local and includes I/O overhead.

bounds_questions.question: Can a power-law convergence claim be inferred from this three-tolerance sample?
bounds_questions.answer: No. r0/r1 errors and counts are identical; no convergence order is plotted or estimated.
